# Kan man investere i verdens undergang?

**Feed**: store-penge  
**Published**: 2026-09-10  
**Market Sentiment**: Mixed

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

This Danish episode of Store Penge features host Michael Bo Mogensen, geopolitical analyst Mikkel Rosenvold of Real Vision, and portfolio manager Tobias Storm. They cover the market's fight between AI/tech optimism and three headwinds: oil above $100 on unrest in Hormuz and Yemen, inflation fears and Middle East uncertainty. The guests are constructive on crypto ahead of the Clarity Act vote. Most of the episode is about AI-doom risk; after that, Tobias makes a long-term case for geothermal energy to power data centres (Fervo, Ormat), the guests call banks attractive for their capex-boom and rate-volatility margins, and Mikkel makes a buy case for Huntington Ingalls and a base case of going short oil in a week or two.

---

## Universe Stocks

### 🟢 HII — Huntington Ingalls Industries | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 70%

Only US carrier builder; the carrier shortage is exposed, and Mikkel expects new orders to be announced before or after the midterms.

#### Reasoning

Guest Mikkel Rosenvold argues the US Navy has only 2-4 active carriers. The USS Abraham Lincoln is worn out after 9 months deployed, and Washington is waking up to the Taiwan/Hormuz dilemma. He expects the carrier programme to accelerate, and HII is the sole supplier, with production that cannot be moved outside the US. The stock has fallen this year, which he sees as a good entry point.

#### Sell Triggers

- if no carrier programme acceleration is announced around the midterms
- if the defence budget is cut
- if orders go to other yards

> *"Så jeg tror, det er en meget god aktie, den er faldet en del i år."*

---

### 🟠 ORA — Ormat Technologies | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 40%

Tobias is researching geothermal as a 24/7 power source for data centres; Ormat is the established player.

#### Reasoning

Guest Tobias Storm sees geothermal as a potential major theme. It is baseload power that needs no batteries and can be sited away from people. Google's investment in Fervo validates the theme, and interest from more hyperscalers could re-rate the sector. Ormat is the established player using older technology. Tobias is still researching and may make it a future portfolio bet.

#### Sell Triggers

- if hyperscalers do not sign geothermal contracts
- if data-centre power demand growth slows
- if drilling costs stay prohibitive

> *"så derfor er det en sektor, som jeg sidder og nørder en del her lige nu"*

---

### 🟡 DANSKE — Danske Bank | **HOLD** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 50%

The guests are positive on banks: capex-boom financing, volatile rates widening margins, and AI cost savings.

#### Reasoning

Asked whether banks have peaked, Mikkel says the sector is generally attractive in Europe and the US. The capex boom brings financing fees, rate volatility lets banks widen net interest margins, and AI can cut credit and compliance headcount. Tobias adds that banks diversify away from tech exposure. The view is general to the sector; Danske Bank is cited as having done well.

#### Sell Triggers

- if rate volatility subsides and margins compress
- if the capex boom stalls
- if credit losses rise

> *"Så jeg synes, at banksektoren er generelt spændende, både i Europa og USA i virkeligheden."*
